synopsis: RadaRays measured 7.8–18.8 milliseconds per polar radar image on an NVIDIA RTX 2070 Super as initial rays increased from 80,000 to 400,000 [f4936]. The glossary repeats this GPU timing range and compares it with 25.8–78.5 milliseconds on a desktop CPU [f16196]. At 160,000 initial rays, the GPU took 10.2 milliseconds versus 39.3 milliseconds on a Ryzen 7 3800X CPU [f4938]. These measurements apply only to the tested radar, model and scene, limiting their use as general performance predictions [f4936, f4938].

relations.note: Both report the same RTX 2070 Super timing range; glossary adds CPU comparison.
Provides a specific ray-count benchmark and identifies the comparison CPU.
Adds the 160,000-ray timing within the reported GPU performance range.
